A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMAD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original MPE and MAMuJoCo experiments, including benchmark returns, exploration measurements, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a Gaussian-policy comparison, HalfCheetah sensitivity experiments, and 10-agent Cooperative Navigation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the proposed objectives in Equations 11-15 retain the same decentralized diffusion policies, centralized distributional critic, synchronized optimization, and temperature tuning. Expanded explanations and the added Gaussian-policy control do not revise OMAD itself.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3.3 adds 10-agent Cooperative Navigation, extending the existing 3- and 4-agent scenarios to a denser coordination problem. The HalfCheetah 6 × 1 task used for new ablations was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix D.3.1 adds an evaluated standard Gaussian-policy comparator on 3-agent Cooperative Navigation. HATD3, HASAC, MADPMD, and MASDAC remain the benchmark comparators; applying that same set to the new 10-agent scenario does not introduce additional methods.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 changes the stated coverage-grid interval from 0.5 to 1.0, specifying integer centers and half-unit boundaries yielding 38 × 36 bins. This corrects the reported protocol without establishing that the experiment was rerun. New HalfCheetah sweeps also specify additional settings, including Vmax values from 2000 to 4000.

E4.justification: The appendix substantially expands diagnostic validation: a Gaussian-policy comparison tests the contribution of policy expressiveness, Tables 4-6 extend atom-count, value-bound, and entropy-coefficient sensitivity tests to HalfCheetah, and Table 7 adds an agent-scaling check. The original Ant ablations, exploration analysis, and qualitative demonstrations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeds, retain the ten-episode evaluation description, and report means with standard deviations. The additional results continue the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no changed run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The original learning curves and all numerical entries in Table 3 remain unchanged. Added outcomes include Gaussian-policy return -26.1 ± 2.9, HalfCheetah sensitivity results in Tables 4-6, and 10-agent OMAD return -445.1 ± 3.3 in Table 7. These are additional experimental results, rather than revised scores for the original comparisons.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the Bellman residual by moving the immediate reward outside the discount factor. The entropy lower-bound theorem and synchronized-objective derivation remain substantively unchanged; the added explanation of trajectory expectations does not introduce a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions: online off-policy diffusion MARL, a tractable entropy surrogate, and coordinated optimization through a joint distributional critic. The headline claims of state-of-the-art performance across 10 tasks and 2.5-5× sample efficiency also remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit discussion of large-agent scalability limits, serial inference versus parallel memory costs, and the argument that sample efficiency offsets denoising overhead. It also explains the exclusion of SMAC. The continuous-action scope and concerns about the ELBO approximation gap were already present in v1.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds a code-access pointer. Appendix D.2 clarifies that the already reported rho = 0 produces hard target-network updates, and Appendix B expands the explanation of sampled diffusion trajectories and tractable Gaussian transitions. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds discussion and citations concerning diffusion-based global-state inference and algorithm-agnostic generative policies, including GORL, and sharpens the online/off-policy positioning. The former anonymous HAQO reference is updated to Lin and Lee's publication of the same work.

P1.justification: v2 removes a duplicated introduction paragraph, expands selected method and appendix explanations, adds an acknowledgement, and divides Appendix D.3 into four named subsections. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The spacious single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference main text with extensively reflowed equations, captions, and figure placement. Figures 3-6 are reduced to column width, Figure 1 gains data-flow labels, and four new appendix tables are added. Existing experimental figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added policy comparison, cross-task sensitivity tests, and 10-agent experiment provide useful support beyond v1's validation. Correcting the Bellman residual and grid specification, clarifying implementation details, and documenting code access also improve the paper. The gains remain limited because some new control and scalability settings are under-specified, while the original benchmark evidence and principal conclusions are unchanged.
